name: T2K
summary: T2K sends an off-axis muon-neutrino or antineutrino beam from J-PARC to Super-Kamiokande, measuring disappearance and electron-flavour appearance over 295 km.
physics_targets: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections and sterile-neutrino tests
detection_principle: Near detectors characterize the beam and neutrino interactions before oscillation. At the far detector, charged particles in ultrapure water produce Cherenkov rings that distinguish electron-like showers from muon-like tracks. Neutrino and antineutrino spectra constrain oscillation parameters.

results.summary: Measured explicit flavour appearance and precision muon-flavour disappearance, providing sensitivity to the CP phase when neutrino and antineutrino data are compared.

The first joint NOvA-T2K fit sharpened oscillation constraints but found no strong preference for either mass ordering. Its CP-violation interpretation is conditional on the ordering and the three-flavour framework.
